items.name: ai-chat
items.title: AI Chat
items.description: The layout for a chat UI: a message log that sticks to the bottom while replies stream unless the reader scrolls up, a jump-to-latest button, an empty state with suggestions and a footer.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

ai.summary: Layout only: <Chat> (a full-height column) > <ChatMessages> (role=log, auto-scroll) + <ChatFooter>. Put ai-message items inside ChatMessages and a prompt-input inside ChatFooter. It holds no chat state, so any source works (Vercel AI SDK useChat, your own fetch stream).
whenToUse: Building an assistant, support bot or copilot panel from ai-message and prompt-input
Any log that receives streaming content and should follow the newest line unless the reader scrolls up
A first-run screen with suggested prompts (ChatEmpty + ChatSuggestions)
whenNotToUse: A single one-off AI answer on a page (use ai-message or streaming-text alone)
Terminal-style command output (use terminal)

a11y.action: Focuses the message log (scroll with arrow keys / Page Up / Page Down), then the jump-to-latest button when shown
On a suggestion, sends it through onSelect
The log is role=log with aria-live=polite; set aria-busy on ChatMessages while a reply streams to avoid announcing every token

customization: Give Chat (or its parent) a height; ChatMessages fills the remaining space and scrolls
contentClassName on ChatMessages and ChatFooter sets the message column width (max-w-3xl by default)
useChatScroll() inside Chat returns { isAtBottom, scrollToBottom } — call scrollToBottom() when the user sends a message
Keep ChatMessages mounted and render ChatEmpty inside it when there are no messages

AI SDK wiring: const { messages, sendMessage, status, stop } = useChat(); render messages in ChatMessages and <PromptInput status={status === 'streaming' || status === 'submitted' ? 'streaming' : 'idle'} onStop={stop} onSubmit={(text) => sendMessage({ text })} /> in ChatFooter

items.name: ai-message
items.title: AI Message
items.description: A chat message with user, assistant and system roles: right-aligned user bubbles, full-width assistant prose, an avatar slot, hover-revealed actions and a hydration-safe timestamp.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

ai.summary: Render one chat turn. <Message role> wraps <MessageAvatar>, <MessageContent>, <MessageActions> (with <MessageAction label> and <MessageCopyAction value>) and <MessageTimestamp date>. It takes plain children, so it works with the Vercel AI SDK, LangChain or any stream.
whenToUse: Rendering each turn of an assistant or chatbot conversation
Showing copy, regenerate and feedback buttons under an assistant reply
A system note inside a conversation, such as 'Model switched to a smaller context window'
whenNotToUse: The scrolling conversation layout itself (use ai-chat and put messages inside ChatMessages)
Threaded comments or email-style lists where both sides look alike

a11y.action: Moves through the action buttons; focusing any of them reveals the action row
Runs the focused action

customization: role: user | assistant | system (sets alignment and bubble styling through context)
MessageActions visibility: hover (default; always visible on touch devices) | always
MessageAction requires a label (used as aria-label and title); pass aria-pressed for thumbs up/down
MessageTimestamp formats with locale (en-US default) and timeZone; without timeZone it formats after hydration in the viewer's zone, or pass preformatted children
Render markdown yourself inside MessageContent; it styles lists, code and spacing lightly
AI SDK: messages.map(m => <Message key={m.id} role={m.role}><MessageContent>{m.parts.map(p => p.type === 'text' ? p.text : null)}</MessageContent></Message>)

changelog.note: Labels (show, hide, copy, regenerate) come from the i18n messages, padding uses start/end so the field mirrors in right-to-left, and the key stays left-to-right. Adds the i18n helper.

ai.summary: Show an existing secret: <ApiKeyField value={key} label='Secret key' onRegenerate={confirmThenRotate} />. It is read-only; copy always copies the full value, even while masked.
whenToUse: API keys, webhook signing secrets and access tokens on settings or developer pages
Showing a newly created key once so the user can copy it
whenNotToUse: Password entry (use an input with type=password)
Secrets you should not send to the browser at all (show only the last four characters from the server)

a11y.action: Moves between reveal, copy and regenerate buttons
Reveal is a toggle button (aria-pressed); copy announces 'Key copied to clipboard'
While masked, screen readers hear the prefix and last characters, not bullet characters

customization: visiblePrefix (default 8) and visibleSuffix (default 4) characters stay visible; the mask length is fixed so it doesn't reveal the key length
onRegenerate shows a regenerate button; confirmation is the caller's job (e.g. a dialog); regenerating spins it
onCopy runs after a successful copy; the component never logs the value

items.name: app-window
items.title: App Window
items.description: The window chrome of a real desktop app (Tauri or Electron): a title bar that drags the window, double-click to maximize, and the controls the platform draws: traffic lights, Windows caption buttons, or none.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

changelog.note: macOS traffic lights are 12 px apart so every target meets the 24 px target-size rule (WCAG 2.5.8).
First release.

ai.summary: Real window chrome for a Tauri or Electron app. <AppWindow onClose onMinimize onMaximize><AppWindowTitleBar title="…">toolbar</AppWindowTitleBar><AppWindowContent/></AppWindow>. It draws the platform's controls (macOS traffic lights on the left, Windows caption buttons on the right, none on iOS or web) from the page's feel, drags the window, and maximizes on double-click. You wire the callbacks; there is no Tauri or Electron dependency.
whenToUse: The window of a Tauri or Electron app with a hidden native title bar (decorations: false, or titleBarStyle hidden)
A desktop-style web app that should match the platform's window chrome
whenNotToUse: Landing-page mockups of a Mac app (use mac-window)
Modal dialogs inside a web app (use dialog)

a11y.action: Reaches the window controls when their handlers are set, then the toolbar
Presses the focused window control
Maximizes or restores (calls onMaximize)

customization: feel: 'macos' | 'windows' | 'ios' | 'web' overrides the page's feel for this window
active: defaults to following real window focus; maximized switches the Windows button to restore and squares the corners
onFullscreen: the macOS green button; hold Option to call onMaximize instead
Tauri v2: onClose={() => getCurrentWindow().close()}; Electron: send an IPC message from the handler
AppWindowControls renders only the controls, for a custom title bar

items.name: comments-1
items.title: Comments 1: threaded discussion
items.description: A threaded discussion: a composer where @ offers people, replies, emoji reactions that count and toggle, editing and deleting your own, resolving a thread, and a comment that appears at once and stays with Retry if it cannot be saved.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

ai.summary: Threaded comments. <Comments1 comments={[{ id, author, body, at: ISO, reactions: { '👍': ['Priya Shah'] }, edited, resolvedBy, replies: [...] }]} people={[{ id, name }]} me='Sam Okafor' now='2026-10-18T10:00:00Z' onPost={({ body, replyTo }) => Promise} onEdit onDelete onReact={(id, emoji, on) => ...} onResolve={(id, resolved) => ...} />. Typing @ opens a people list (arrows, Enter or Tab pick, Escape closes); only @Name that matches a person is highlighted. Times are 'N min ago' from now; pass now yourself, the block never reads the clock. Only comments whose author equals me can be edited or deleted. Reject onPost to show Not posted with Retry.
whenToUse: Comments on a document, task, design or post
A team discussion with mentions and reactions
whenNotToUse: Real-time chat (use chat-1)
A support conversation with private notes (use tickets-1)

a11y.keys: @, Up / Down, Enter or Tab, Escape
a11y.action: The composer is a combobox; the people list is a listbox with the active option announced, and Escape closes it without losing the text
Each is a toggle button that says its emoji, count and who reacted ('👍 3: Priya Shah, Sam Okafor, Theo Nakamura')
Edit and Delete say which comment they act on; posting, replying, deleting and resolving are announced politely

customization: Replies nest one level deep, drawn with a rule on the reading edge so it mirrors in right-to-left
A resolved thread collapses to one line with Show, and Reopen brings it back
Your own comments get Edit and Delete; reactions toggle for you

items.name: desktop-1
items.title: Desktop 1: preferences window
items.description: The Settings window of a Tauri or Electron app: toolbar tabs on macOS, a side nav with setting cards on Windows. Launch at login, menu bar, appearance, a global shortcut recorder and update settings that apply as they change.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

changelog.note: The shortcut formatting and recording moved into the shortcut lib item, which this block now installs. formatShortcut is still exported from here; behaviour is unchanged.
First release.

ai.summary: A complete preferences window. <Desktop1 appName defaultValues onValuesChange={(v) => persist(v)} onCheckForUpdates />. Panes: General, Appearance, Shortcuts (a key-combination recorder that writes ⇧⌘Space on a Mac and Ctrl+Shift+Space on Windows), Updates, Advanced, plus extraPanes. Layout follows the feel: toolbar tabs and a pane-named title on macOS, side nav and setting cards on Windows.
whenToUse: The Settings or Preferences window of a Tauri or Electron app
A desktop-style web app that needs app-level preferences
whenNotToUse: Account settings saved with a button (use settings-1)
A settings page inside a web app's layout (use settings-2 or settings-panel)

a11y.action: Move between panes (left and right on macOS, up and down in the Windows side nav); right-to-left swaps them
Starts recording; the next combination with a modifier is saved, Escape cancels, Delete clears
Every switch, segmented control and select is labelled by its row

customization: frame={false} drops the window chrome inside a real native window
values + onValuesChange to control it; shortcut strings use Mod for ⌘ or Ctrl, e.g. 'Mod+Shift+Space'
extraPanes=[{ id, label, icon, content }]; formatShortcut(shortcut, feel) is exported for your menus
Tauri: pass the shortcut to @tauri-apps/plugin-global-shortcut (replace Mod with CommandOrControl)

meta.statesNone: Settings apply the moment they change, as desktop apps do: nothing to load, submit or fail.

items.description: The panel of a menu bar app on macOS or a tray flyout on Windows: a clipboard history with search, pins, a pause switch, keyboard selection and Preferences and Quit, with loading, empty and error states.

ai.summary: A status-item app panel. <Desktop2 appName items={[{ id, text, kind: 'text' | 'link' | 'code' | 'color', source, time, pinned }]} onCopy onTogglePin onClear onOpenPreferences onQuit />. frame draws a menu bar slice (macOS) or taskbar (Windows) around it for marketing pages; frame={false} renders only the panel for the real tray window. Swap the list for your own content by forking the file: the header, search, listbox and footer are separate parts.

Showing a menu bar utility on its landing page
whenNotToUse: Command search across an app (use command or spotlight-search)
A plain dropdown menu (use dropdown-menu)

a11y.action: Moves through the history (a combobox with a listbox); the item is announced
Copies the selected item; "Copied" is announced
Pins or unpins the selected item

customization: feel: 'macos' | 'windows' (defaults to the page's feel); macOS draws menu-style footer rows, Windows icon buttons
paused + onPausedChange control the recording switch
Tauri: open it with a tray icon (tray-icon feature) and a borderless, transparent window, then render frame={false}
state, onRetry, emptyState and errorState as in every Ballmac block with states

states.note: Skeleton rows the shape of history items, announced as loading; search and Clear are disabled.

items.name: desktop-3
items.title: Desktop 3: software update
items.description: The update window of a desktop app, the whole cycle: checking, a new version with release notes, downloading with progress, ready to relaunch, up to date and failed. Buttons follow each platform's order and wording.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

ai.summary: An updater window. Leave state out and it runs itself: <Desktop3 currentVersion releases={[{ version, date, changes: [{ type: 'new' | 'improved' | 'fixed', text }] }]} onInstall={async (report) => { …; report(0.5) }} onRelaunch onSkip onRemindLater />. Or drive it from your updater with state (loading = checking, submitting + progress = downloading, success = ready, empty = up to date, error). macOS: Title Case buttons, default button last. Windows: sentence case, default button first.
whenToUse: The update prompt of a Tauri app (tauri-plugin-updater) or an Electron app (electron-updater)
A changelog-style "what's new" window after an update
whenNotToUse: A public changelog page (use changelog-1)
A small in-app banner that an update exists (use banner)

a11y.action: Each stage's heading is announced politely; the byte count is not, so it does not chatter
The notes region scrolls with the arrow keys
Buttons are in the platform's visual order, so focus order matches what people see

customization: feel: 'macos' | 'windows' (defaults to the page's feel); frame={false} inside a real native window
Tauri: const update = await check(); onInstall={(report) => update.downloadAndInstall((e) => …report(done / total))}; onRelaunch={() => relaunch()}
Electron: map autoUpdater's checking-for-update, download-progress, update-downloaded and error events onto state and progress; onRelaunch={() => autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()}
automatic + onAutomaticChange control the checkbox; size is the download size in bytes

states.title: Checking
states.note: A spinner and "Checking for updates…" with the current version; marked busy.

states.title: Downloading
states.note: A progress bar with megabytes done of the total; the release notes stay readable and Hide keeps it going in the background.

states.title: Ready to relaunch
states.note: "Install and Relaunch" (macOS) or "Restart now" (Windows) calls onRelaunch; the other button installs on quit.

states.title: Up to date
states.note: Says the current version is the newest, with OK.

states.title: Download failed
states.note: Says nothing was changed and offers Try Again (onRetry); errorState sets the copy.

items.name: desktop-4
items.title: Desktop 4: licence activation
items.description: Licence activation for a paid desktop app: a trial meter, a key field that cleans up pasted keys, activation that shows why a key failed, the licensed view with deactivate, and a trial-ended mode.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

ai.summary: A licence window. <Desktop4 appName trialDaysLeft trialLength buyUrl onActivate={async (key) => { const r = await validate(key); if (!r.ok) throw new Error(r.reason); return { licensedTo: r.email, plan: 'Pro' } }} onContinueTrial onDeactivate />. trialDaysLeft={0} switches to the trial-ended mode with Quit instead of Continue. Pass licence to open on the licensed view.
whenToUse: Activating a paid Tauri or Electron app with a licence key (Dodo Payments, Lemon Squeezy, Keygen, Paddle)
The window shown when a trial ends
whenNotToUse: Web subscriptions with sign-in (use billing-1 or pricing blocks)
Entering a one-time code (use verify-1 or input-otp)

a11y.action: Activates; the field is labelled and its error is linked with aria-describedby
The reason is announced as an alert and the field is marked invalid
The activated heading is announced politely

customization: feel: 'macos' | 'windows' (defaults to the page's feel); wording follows it ("this Mac", "this PC") and macOS uses Title Case buttons
seatsNote: one line under the field, e.g. "One licence works on up to 3 Macs."
Dodo Payments: call /licenses/activate from your backend or Tauri command with the key and a device name, then store the instance id for deactivate
state: "submitting" | "success" | "error" to drive it yourself; leave it out and it runs itself

states.title: Activating
states.note: The field goes read-only and Activate shows a spinner and "Activating…"; announced politely.

states.title: Activated
states.note: Who it is licensed to and on which device, with Done and, when onDeactivate is set, Deactivate.

states.title: Key refused
states.note: The reason under the field, announced as an alert and linked to it; errorState.description sets it. Thrown Error messages from onActivate show the same way.

items.description: A developers page: a 14-day request chart with errors stacked, success rate and median time, API keys shown in full once and revoked behind a confirmation, and a request log with filter, responses and copy as curl.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

ai.summary: A developer dashboard page. <Dev1 keys={[{ id, name, scope: 'read' | 'write' | 'admin', last4, created, lastUsed }]} usage={{ days: [{ label, ok, errors }], p50 }} requests={[{ id, method, path, status, ms, time, ip, keyName, response }]} baseUrl onCreateKey={async ({ name, scope, env }) => ({ id, secret })} onRevokeKey onEnvChange defaultEnv />. The secret returned by onCreateKey is shown once in a copy banner and only its last four characters are kept in the list.
whenToUse: The developer or API section of a platform product

a11y.action: An image with a text summary, plus a hidden table with the numbers for each day; bars never carry meaning by color alone

Opens its response (aria-expanded); status is an icon, the number and words, not color alone

customization: baseUrl for the curl commands; defaultEnv: 'test' | 'live' (live shows a warning and sk_live_ prefixes)
onCreateKey must call your backend: the secret must never be derivable on the client
defaultOpenRequest opens a request at first

ai.summary: A Markdown editor. <Editor1 title defaultValue autosaveMs={1200} onSave={(value) => Promise} onChange={(value) => ...} defaultTab='write' | 'preview' />. Supports headings (1 to 3), bold, italic, inline code, links (http, https, mailto only), bulleted and numbered lists, quotes and rules. Ctrl or Command with B, I, K format and S saves now. A labelled region updated as you type; on narrow screens a Write and Preview tablist switches between the two

customization: The writing field uses dir=auto, so Arabic and Hebrew text flow the right way as you type
Formatting marks wrap the selection, or a placeholder that is selected so typing replaces it
Reading time assumes 220 words a minute

ai.summary: A/B test results. <Experiments1 title hypothesis metric status variants={[{ id, name, visitors, conversions, control?: true }]} confidence={0.95} onShip={(variant) => ...} />. Pass raw counts: rates, Wilson 95% intervals, relative lift, chance to beat the control (normal approximation), a two-sided p-value and the verdict are worked out. The verdict is a winner (p below 1 minus confidence), a loser, 'not enough data' with the visitors still needed at 80% power, or 'no clear difference'.
whenToUse: An experimentation or growth tool showing test results

whenNotToUse: Plain KPI cards (use stats-1 or a dashboard block)

Marked with a word and an icon as well as color; losses are written as lift in words, such as -4.2% vs control

customization: confidence: 0.8 to 0.99 sets how sure to be before calling a winner
The interval axis runs left to right in every language, like a chart
All statistics are deterministic, so server and client agree

items.description: A project timeline: bars placed by real dates with a progress fill, milestones, dependency arrows, a today line, three zoom levels, a sticky task column, a details panel and a table of the same data for screen readers.

ai.summary: A Gantt chart. <Gantt1 tasks={[{ id, name, start: '2026-10-05', end: '2026-10-16', progress: 0..1, group, owner, dependsOn: ['id'], milestone }]} today="2026-10-18" defaultScale='days' | 'weeks' | 'months' defaultSelectedId locale onSelect />. Status is worked out for you: done at progress 1, late when the end date has passed, in progress when it has started, planned otherwise. Pass today yourself (an ISO date); the block never reads the clock. A milestone has the same start and end.

dependsOn draws arrows; a task that starts before what it depends on shows the arrow running backwards, which is the sign of a planning problem

items.name: goals-1
items.title: Goals 1: objectives and key results
items.description: Objectives and key results for a period: progress worked out from start, current and target, a pace mark on each bar for where it should be today, on track, at risk or behind in words, overall progress, team filter and in-place updates.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

ai.summary: OKRs. <Goals1 objectives={[{ id, title, owner, team, keyResults: [{ id, title, start, target, current, unit, prefix }] }]} period='Q4 2026' range={['2026-10-01', '2026-12-31']} today='2026-11-12' locale onUpdate={(objective, keyResult, value) => Promise} />. Key result progress is (current - start) / (target - start), clamped 0 to 1, so a target below the start means lower is better. Status compares progress with the share of the period gone: within 10 points On track, within 25 At risk, else Behind, 100% Done. Pass today yourself; the block never reads the clock. Reject onUpdate and the old value returns with the message.
whenToUse: A team or company goals page
A quarterly review dashboard
whenNotToUse: A project plan with dates and dependencies (use gantt-1)
A list of to-dos (use tasks-1)

a11y.action: Each key result has an Update button named for it; Enter saves the number and Escape cancels
Written as On track, At risk, Behind or Done with an icon and the percentage, never by color alone; the pace mark is explained in a caption
Counts by status are a labelled list ('2 On track, 1 At risk')

customization: unit goes after the number ('%', ' ms') and prefix before it ('$')
Lower-is-better results are recognised from target < start and say so
The bars, ring and pace marks mirror in right-to-left

items.name: import-1
items.title: Import 1: CSV import with column matching
items.description: A data import in four steps: choose a CSV, match its columns to your fields (found for you where names are alike), review which rows are ready and which have problems and why, then import with progress and a summary.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

ai.summary: A CSV importer. <Import1 fields={[{ key, label, required, aliases: ['e-mail'], validate: (value) => string | null }]} sampleCsv onImport={(rows, progress) => Promise} defaultStep />. Columns are matched by key, label and aliases; required fields must be matched; each row is checked for missing required values, validate() reasons and duplicate emails; only passing rows reach onImport, which can call progress(done). Reject onImport to show its message and keep the rows. Without onImport a run is simulated.
whenToUse: Importing contacts, products or users from a spreadsheet
Migrating data from another tool
whenNotToUse: Uploading files of any kind (use upload-1)
Editing rows in place (use a data table)

a11y.action: An ordered list that marks the current step and each finished one in words; focus moves to the new step's heading
Each field's menu is labelled with the field name and says (required); a sample of the matched values shows beside it
A real table with a caption; every row says Ready or lists its problems in words beside an icon, not only by color

customization: fields decide what can be imported, how it is checked and what other column names match it
A CSV reader handles quotes, commas and line breaks inside quotes
Choosing a file works by drag, click or the sample button, and a wrong file type says how to export a CSV

items.name: inventory-1
items.title: Inventory 1: stock levels and reordering
items.description: A stock overview: stock value, lines low or out, units on the way, and every item with a bar against its reorder point, days of cover at today's pace, status in words, and an order form that suggests how many to buy.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

ai.summary: A stock overview. <Inventory1 items={[{ id, sku, name, category, onHand, reorderAt, perDay, cost, incoming: { qty, eta } }]} currency locale onReorder={(item, qty) => Promise} />. Status is Out of stock (0), Low (at or under reorderAt), Plenty (over four times reorderAt) or In stock; days left is onHand divided by perDay; stock value is onHand times cost. The suggested order is two reorder points plus fourteen days of sales, minus what is on hand and on the way. Reject onReorder to show the reason; nothing is marked as ordered.
whenToUse: An ecommerce or warehouse admin: what to reorder first
A restaurant or retail back office
whenNotToUse: A customer-facing product page
Order history (use a data table)

a11y.action: Each Reorder button names its product; the order form field is labelled and focused when it opens, and a placed order is announced
Out of stock, Low, In stock and Plenty are written beside an icon, and 'N days left' is text; the bar has a text equivalent giving on hand and the reorder point
Buttons say whether they are on and show counts; the number of products shown is announced politely

customization: SKUs are shown left to right in right-to-left layouts, like codes
The mark on each bar is the reorder point
Sorting by days left puts what will run out first at the top

items.name: poll-1
items.title: Poll 1: vote and live results
items.description: A poll: pick one option or several, vote, and results appear with each share, the leader marked and your choice highlighted. Your vote counts at once and is taken back with the reason if it fails; change it until the poll closes.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

ai.summary: A poll. <Poll1 question description options={[{ id, label, votes, hint }]} multiple maxChoices={2} closesAt='2026-10-20T18:00:00Z' now='2026-10-18T10:00:00Z' defaultVoted={['a']} onVote={(ids) => Promise} />. Before voting people choose (radio buttons, or checkboxes with multiple); after voting, or when closed, they see each share, the single leader and their own choice. Votes are counted at once; reject onVote and they are taken back with the message. Changing a vote removes the old choice and adds the new. Time left comes from closesAt and now; pass now yourself, the block never reads the clock.
whenToUse: Letting users vote on what to build next
Community and event polls with live results
whenNotToUse: A multi-question survey (use survey-1)
Scored questions with right answers (use quiz-1)

a11y.action: Options are real radio buttons (or checkboxes when several are allowed); when the limit is reached the rest are disabled and the legend says the limit
Each option reads as its label, percentage and vote count; your choice says Your vote and the leader says Leading, with icons and words, not only color
A counted vote is announced politely; a failure is an alert that says it was taken back

customization: multiple and maxChoices allow several choices
Leading is shown only when one option is ahead
See results without voting reveals the bars and offers Vote now

states.title: Loading
states.note: A skeleton question and options, announced as loading.

states.title: No poll
states.note: Says a question appears here when there is one to vote on; emptyState sets the copy.

states.title: Could not load
states.note: An alert saying your vote has not been lost, with Try again (onRetry). A vote that fails to save is taken back with its reason in place.

items.description: An investment portfolio: total value and its change over a week, month or year, a line you scrub by pointer or arrow keys, an allocation ring, and sortable holdings with price, share, day change and a small trend line.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

ai.summary: An investment portfolio. <Portfolio1 holdings={[{ id, symbol, name, kind: 'Stocks', shares, price, dayPct, spark: number[] }]} series={{ '1W': number[], '1M': number[], '1Y': number[] }} currency='USD' locale defaultRange='1M' />. Total value, allocation by kind, each holding's share and today's gain are worked out from holdings; the change over the range comes from the first and last point of the series. The line is a slider (Left, Right, Home, End) that reads out any point. Gains and losses carry a sign and an arrow as well as color.
whenToUse: An investing or wealth app's overview
A finance dashboard showing what is held and how it is doing
whenNotToUse: A trading screen with order entry
A single stock price chart with candles

a11y.keys: Tab, then Left / Right / Home / End
a11y.action: The value line is a slider; its value text reads the amount and 'point 12 of 30', and a pointer shows the same on hover
Column headers are buttons with aria-sort; type filters say whether they are on; the table is a captioned, focusable region that scrolls on phones
Written as '+0.82%' or '−0.34%' with an up or down arrow, never by color alone; the ring has a text equivalent listing each share

customization: series can hold any of the three ranges; a missing one falls back to the month
currency and locale format every amount
The chart and ring keep their direction in right-to-left, like any chart

Each step reads 'Step 2.' first, and the current one is outlined as well as numbered

customization: serves is the base the amounts are written for
Countable ingredients (eggs) round to a sensible fraction or one decimal
The timer ring and the hero mirror in right-to-left

items.title: Tickets 1: support ticket
items.description: One support ticket as an agent sees it: replies and private notes, a reply timer, a composer that switches between Reply and Internal note with canned replies, and a side panel for the customer, assignee, status and priority.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

ai.summary: A support ticket. <Tickets1 ticket={{ id, number, subject, status: 'open' | 'pending' | 'solved', priority: 'low' | 'normal' | 'high' | 'urgent', assignee, tags, replyDueAt: ISO, requester: { name, email, plan, location, since }, messages: [{ id, from: 'customer' | 'agent' | 'note', author, time, body }] }} agents cannedReplies now='2026-10-18T10:42:00Z' me onSend={({ kind: 'reply' | 'note', body }) => Promise} onStatusChange onPriorityChange onAssign />. The reply timer shows only while the last message is from the customer; it says time left, or how late. A sent reply sets the status to Waiting on customer. Reject onSend and the message stays with Retry. Pass now yourself; the block never reads the clock.
whenToUse: A helpdesk or support tool's ticket view
An internal request or approval thread with private notes
whenNotToUse: A live chat widget (use chat-1)
A public help center (use help-1)

a11y.action: Reply and Internal note are tabs; the composer sends with the button or the shortcut, and the field is named for what it will do
Private notes are dashed, tinted and say 'Internal note, only your team sees this' in words, so they are never mistaken for a reply
'Reply due in 48 min' or 'Reply is 35 min late' is a live region with an icon, not only a color

customization: Messages you send appear at once with Sending, then settle; a failure shows Not sent and Retry in place
Canned replies insert into the draft without replacing it
Your messages sit on the reading end and mirror in right-to-left

customization: dayTarget sets what a full day is (weekends are not counted against the week target)

ai.summary: Wrap any Recharts chart: <ChartFrame title description data xKey series={[{ key, label }]}>{(chart) => <LineChart>…</LineChart>}</ChartFrame>. Use chart.color(key) for strokes, chart.fill(key) for fills, chart.isHidden(key) for `hide`, chart.defs in <defs>, chart.animate for isAnimationActive and chart.rtl to reverse the x axis. The frame adds a Chart/Table switch, a CSV download, a toggling legend, optional patterns, a written summary and state handling. Prefer the ready-made ChartArea, ChartBar, ChartLine, ChartPie, ChartRadar, ChartRadial or ChartScatter when one fits.

whenNotToUse: A tiny inline trend (use sparkline)

The figure has a name and a summary written from the data (first to last, highest and lowest, or a ranking); pass summary to say what it means
Series are filled with stripes, dots and hatching as well as color, so color is never the only signal

customization: aspect: video | wide | panorama | square | tall
valueFormatter and categoryFormatter write numbers and categories everywhere
table: your own columns for charts whose data is not one column per series

items.title: Code Block
items.description: A code panel with filename and language header, line numbers, highlighted lines, a wrap toggle, copy feedback and file tabs. No highlighter bundled; pass Shiki output as children.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

changelog.note: Adds the compound API of shadcn's Code Block: header, title, actions, copy button, content, line and footer parts, size and variant, diff and highlighted lines, start line and a useHighlightedCode hook. The ready-made panel and CodeBlockTabs are unchanged.

ai.summary: Two ways to use it. Ready-made: <CodeBlock code filename language lineNumbers highlight={[2,3]} /> renders plain monospace text. Compound (the same API as shadcn's Code Block, so chat kits and agent output drop in): <CodeBlock size variant><CodeBlockHeader><CodeBlockTitle/><CodeBlockActions><CodeBlockCopyButton value/></CodeBlockActions></CodeBlockHeader><CodeBlockContent lineNumbers wrap startLine><CodeBlockLine variant="added|removed|highlighted"/></CodeBlockContent><CodeBlockFooter/></CodeBlock>, with useHighlightedCode(code, language) giving one node per line. For syntax colors, highlight on the server (e.g. Shiki) and pass the result as children plus the raw code for copying. <CodeBlockTabs files={[…]}> shows several files.
whenToUse: Code samples in docs, READMEs rendered on the web and blog posts
Showing a changed file with specific lines highlighted
Several related files (component, usage, config) in one panel with tabs
whenNotToUse: One-line install commands for several package managers (use install-tabs)
Terminal sessions with prompts and output (use terminal)
Editable code (use a code editor)

a11y.action: Focuses the scrollable code region (arrow keys scroll long lines), then wrap and copy buttons
In CodeBlockTabs, moves between file tabs
Copying announces 'Copied to clipboard' through a polite live region

customization: code (plain text) or children (pre-highlighted markup). Line numbers use a CSS counter on .line spans, which is also what Shiki emits
highlight: 1-based line numbers (plain code only; with Shiki use its notation transformers)
wrap (initial) and wrapToggle; copyable={false} hides copy
bodyClassName for a max height, e.g. 'max-h-80'

Compound mode: put CodeBlockHeader, CodeBlockActions, CodeBlockContent or CodeBlockFooter directly inside CodeBlock. size="sm" and variant="destructive" suit tool output and errors; CodeBlockActions without a header floats and shows on hover, focus and touch
Shiki: const html = await codeToHtml(code, { lang, themes }) then <CodeBlock code={code} language={lang}><div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} /></CodeBlock>

items.name: feel-auto
items.title: Feel Auto
items.description: Picks the platform feel for you: macOS, iOS, Windows or web, from the device, before the first paint. All four feels are included and a user's override is remembered.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

[class*=\"focus-visible:ring-[3px]\"]:fo.--tw-ring-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--bm-focus-color, var(--ring)) var(--bm-focus-alpha, 50%), transparent)

[class*=\"focus-within:ring-[3px]\"]:foc.--tw-ring-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--bm-focus-color, var(--ring)) var(--bm-focus-alpha, 50%), transparent)

items.docs: Render <FeelScript /> once in <head> in your root layout and add suppressHydrationWarning to <html>. Use setFeel('macos' | 'ios' | 'windows' | 'web' | 'auto') from @/lib/ballmac/feel to let people choose.

ai.summary: Install once, render <FeelScript /> in <head>, and the whole app handles like the platform it runs on. A Tauri or Electron app on a Mac becomes macOS and the same app on Windows becomes Windows, with no code branches.
whenToUse: Desktop apps (Tauri, Electron) that ship to more than one OS
Web apps that should feel native on phones and desktops
whenNotToUse: Apps that always want one feel: install feel-macos, feel-ios or feel-windows instead
Server components that must not read the platform: the feel is applied on the client before paint
customization: setFeel('auto') returns to the device's own feel
The font is inherited from data-feel on <html>; apps that set their own font on <body> keep it

items.name: state-view
items.title: State View
items.description: Shows the right thing for what the data is doing: a skeleton while loading, a helpful empty state, an error with retry, or your content. Announced to screen readers, never steals focus, fades with the theme's motion.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

changelog.note: Moves frameProps into its own frame-props module so server components can use it; state-view still exports it.
First release.

ai.summary: Wrap any data view: <StateView state={state} loading={<MySkeleton/>} empty={{ title, description, action }} error={{ title, description, details }} onRetry={retry}>{ready content}</StateView>. Pair with useResource, which returns the state. Loading is announced and the region is aria-busy; errors use role=alert; focus is never moved.
whenToUse: Any list, table, feed or panel that loads data
Giving a block its loading, empty and error views without writing them each time
whenNotToUse: Forms: they track submitting and success themselves (blocks with a state prop handle it)
A single value that is just a number: use a skeleton line

a11y.action: Loading is announced as a status; an error is announced as an alert; the region is aria-busy while loading
Reaches the retry button and the details disclosure; focus is never moved for you

customization: loading: pass a skeleton shaped like your content so nothing jumps
empty and error: a config object ({ title, description, icon, action } and { title, description, details, retryLabel, action }) or your own node

items.name: template-goods

items.description: A five-page store with a bag that persists across pages: a collage home, a filterable shop, a product page with glaze and gallery pickers, a bag with a free-shipping meter and promo code, and a validated checkout. Products are drawn in CSS.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>
items.docs: Pages are at /goods, /goods/shop, /goods/shop/[id], /goods/cart and /goods/checkout. Products, glazes and reviews live in goods-data.ts. changelog.note: Hover lift and press depth follow the theme's --bm-lift and --bm-hover tokens. Unchanged by default.
The page that reads params now does so inside Suspense, which Cache Components (the default in new Next.js 16.4 apps) requires. Nothing else changes.

whenToUse: Small online shops and product drops
Any store that needs filters, a product page, a bag and checkout
whenNotToUse: Large catalogues that need server-side search and pagination

a11y.action: A radio group; arrow keys change the glaze and the picture follows
Opens from the header; Escape closes it and focus returns to the button
Each active filter is a button that removes itself

customization: Replace products and reviews in goods-data.ts
Swap the cart store for your cart or commerce API

TerminalLine typing + speed (chars/sec) types a single command; inside TerminalAnimated commands type automatically
TerminalAnimated speed, lineDelay (ms), startDelay (ms), startOnView, onComplete

as: h1 | h2 | h3 | h4 | p | span | div

open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, disabled on TraceCollapsible

items.name: theme
items.title: Ballmac Theme
items.description: Ballmac UI design tokens in OKLCH: colours, radius, chart colours, motion (speed, bounce, travel, hover, stagger) and the platform feel tokens (focus, shadows, text scale, control sizes), with a reduced-motion fallback.
items.author: Ballmac <https://ui.ballmac.com>

[class*=\"focus-visible:ring-[3px]\"]:fo.--tw-ring-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--bm-focus-color, var(--ring)) var(--bm-focus-alpha, 50%), transparent)

[class*=\"focus-within:ring-[3px]\"]:foc.--tw-ring-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--bm-focus-color, var(--ring)) var(--bm-focus-alpha, 50%), transparent)

changelog.note: Adds the platform feel tokens (focus ring, elevation, text scale, control, menu and sidebar sizes) at the web feel, which is what the components already do.
Motion is part of the theme: speed, bounce, travel, hover and stagger drive Tailwind's duration and easing scales, with a reduced-motion fallback.
First release.

ai.summary: Installs Ballmac UI's color, radius and motion tokens as CSS variables. Optional: every Ballmac item also works with any shadcn theme.
whenToUse: Starting a new project that should look like Ballmac UI
Matching the Ballmac demos exactly
whenNotToUse: The project already has a brand theme you want to keep
customization: Change --ring and --chart-1 to your brand color
Adjust --radius for rounder or sharper corners
Change --bm-speed, --bm-bounce, --bm-travel, --bm-hover and --bm-stagger to change how everything moves
Install feel-macos, feel-ios or feel-windows to make everything handle like that platform
